title: coworker_stole_my_parkour_route
display_title: My coworker copied my Minecraft parkour run frame-by-frame and posted it a day early
beats: My coworker (26M) asked me (27F) to 'casually' show him my parkour build during lunch, so I did.
Every jump, every skip pattern, every camera angle -- I walked him through the whole route like an idiot.
Two days later he posts a video with my exact course, my exact timing, even my exact fall at block 40 -- posted the night before mine went live.
I messaged him -- he said 'ideas can't be stolen, only executed better,' and left it on read.
Our team Slack found out and split instantly: half said I was paranoid, half said he was a snake.
Our manager pulled us into a call and just said 'figure it out privately' -- so nothing happened to him.
I posted mine anyway with the original build timestamps proving I built it first, and it's now outperforming his three to one.
He still hasn't apologized, and people keep tagging him in the comments... So, Reddit -- AITAH for exposing him publicly instead of letting it go?
